A bicycle gear system is a mechanism designed to manipulate the mechanical advantage of the rider, allowing you to maintain a consistent effort (cadence) while managing different speeds and inclines. The system works by changing the size of the gears and the length of the chain, effectively altering the ratio between how much force you apply and how much distance the bicycle travels.

The core components are the **chainrings** (the gears attached to the pedals) and the **cassette or freewheel** (the gears on the rear wheel). When you shift gears, you are changing which teeth of the chainring are connected to which teeth of the cassette.
